Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Clinical summary: Adolescent patient with 2 days of lower abdominal pain described as burning and progressive, associated with feeling hot/sweaty and mild nausea. Bowel habits largely normal; pink urine with increased urination; sexual activity ongoing; Implanon contraception in place; last menstrual period about 2 weeks ago. Pregnancy test planned to exclude pregnancy-related etiologies. Empiric antibiotic therapy considered for possible urinary tract infection. Follow-up planned in a few days.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - Urinary tract infection (cystitis) — High
    - Rationale: Lower abdominal/pelvic pain near bladder, pink urine, increased urination; clinician planned empiric antibiotics.
  - Early pregnancy-related pain (including risk of ectopic pregnancy) — Medium-High
    - Rationale: Sexual activity with near-term menstruation context; implant contraception present but not absolute protection; pregnancy test planned.
  - Ovarian cyst (functional corpus luteum or other adnexal cyst) — Medium
    - Rationale: Reproductive-age female with lower abdominal pain.
- Conflicts: No explicit conflicts between transcript and DDx identified.

Management Plan
- Start Trimethoprim today for suspected UTI
  - Trimethoprim — dose/route/frequency: one tablet twice daily for 3 days; route not documented
- Analgesia
  - Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented
- Supportive care
  - Increase fluid intake
  - Cranberry juice (adjunct for urinary symptoms)
- Investigations
  - Pregnancy test planned to rule out pregnancy-related etiologies
- Follow-up
  - Return to clinic in a few days or sooner if symptoms worsen (increasing abdominal pain, fever hot/cold sweats, vomiting, inability to keep fluids)
- Additional instructions
  - Continue antibiotics as prescribed; contact if any new or worsening symptoms
  - Script to pharmacy: proceed with Trimethoprim today
